turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Hi, this is Elena! Thanks for calling back so fast.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Hi Elena, absolutely. I saw your demo request—before we schedule it, how are you training new SDRs today, and how long until they ramp?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Right now I run onboarding myself for four to six new SDRs each quarter, mostly through live role-plays, call recordings, and shadowing experienced reps. It usually takes about six to eight weeks for them to feel comfortable, but I can’t listen to every practice call or clearly show leadership whether the training is working.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: That sounds tough to scale. Where do new reps struggle most during those six to eight weeks, and how are you measuring improvement today?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: They struggle most with confidence on cold calls, especially handling objections and keeping the conversation natural when prospects push back. Today I’m relying on my own notes, manager feedback, and eventually their conversion numbers, but it’s pretty informal—can I see how reps are improving over time?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Yes—managers see weekly progress, and every score cites the exact quote behind it. We can show that in the demo; what timing works?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Oh, interesting—that level of detail would be really helpful. I’d like to see it before the end of the month; could you do Friday at 2 p.m., and how long does setup typically take?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Friday at 2 works; I’ll send the invite. Setup depends on your scenarios and team, and we’ll map that out together.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: That makes sense. I’ll look out for the invite and look forward to seeing it. Great, talk soon!
